questions.question: What is bidirectional RNN in RNN and how does it work?
questions.ideal_answer: bidirectional RNN in RNN refers to future context utilization. It works by two-directional processing. Key characteristics include forward + backward hidden states concatenated. Example: BiLSTM for NER. Common pitfalls include real-time processing limitation.

questions.question: What is recurrent connections in RNN and how does it work?
questions.ideal_answer: recurrent connections in RNN refers to sequential data processing. It works by hidden state persistence. Key characteristics include h_t = tanh(W_hh * h_{t-1} + W_xh * x_t + b). Example: unrolled computation graph. Common pitfalls include temporal dependencies.
